about.title: About
about.bioParagraph: Ilya Medvedev (born 1981) is a Swiss-based contemporary artist and educator whose multidisciplinary practice spans large-scale oil painting, drawing, photography, and site-specific installations. Currently living and working in Basel, Switzerland, Medvedev constructs a raw visual universe that navigates human anatomy, classical traditions, and the psychological realities of the human condition.
about.section1Text1: The foundations of the artistic drive trace back to intense childhood encounters with visual staging and classical form around the age of six. Growing up as the child of a prominent puppet theater director at the Tashkent Puppet Theater, Medvedev spent formative years immersed in an environment of dramatic storytelling, closed rehearsals, and the physical fabrication of figures.
about.section1Text2: Simultaneously, early private creative impulses were sparked by influential books kept in the family home. Medvedev began obsessively copying classical compositions from a book of Rembrandt prints, finding a favorite, recurring motif in the intense imagery of the crucifixion. This was paired with a fascination for raw physical form, driven by sketching nude anatomical plates from a medical textbook, alongside copying the dramatic, textured prehistoric oil paintings of Czech illustrator Zdeněk Burian. These early aesthetic pillars fused a lifelong interest in classical gravity, raw anatomy, and deliberate visual staging.
about.section2Text: Medvedev's mature studio practice operates at the intersection of performance and composition, relying on a process known in contemporary art as working from constructed photographic references. Within the studio, the artist orchestrates complex physical installations using live models, anatomical human skulls, curated still-life elements, and specific props—a process that directly mirrors a childhood familiarity with theatrical assembly. These meticulously staged scenes are documented through precise photography, serving as the definitive visual prototype. Medvedev then translates these captured photographic references onto the final canvas, balancing highly stylized theatrical layouts with a cold, precise execution.
about.section3Text: In direct contrast to the controlled space of the studio, live session drawing serves as a vital, spontaneous pillar of the practice. Medvedev steps out of the traditional workspace to draw in real time within dynamic public environments, including city streets, parks, beaches, and crowded venues. These public sessions prioritize the raw immediacy of the moment. Drawing directly from life establishes an unfiltered, visceral contact with the subject's unique personality. The energetic connection forged between the artist and the individual in that exact window becomes the core meaning of the artwork, capturing fleeting psychological realities that cannot be simulated through secondary or artificial reference material.
about.section4Text1: The technical command and theoretical depth behind this practice were refined through a rigorous, multi-tiered academic path. Medvedev's formal training began with a comprehensive specialization in Byzantine Iconography Painting at the Jerusalem Greek Orthodox Patriarchy, providing a foundational mastery of traditional technical media, precision, and historical glazing techniques. This classical discipline was subsequently expanded into contemporary academic contexts, earning a Bachelor of Education in Fine Arts (B.Ed. FA) from the Beit Berl Art Academy in Kfar Saba, followed by a Master of Fine Arts (MFA) from the prestigious Bezalel Academy of Arts and Design in Jerusalem.
about.section4Text2: Throughout this academic journey and a subsequent five-year period working as a professional tattoo artist, Medvedev's vocabulary continuously evolved. The artist engaged deeply with the deliberately crude, rule-breaking aesthetics of the 'Bad Painting' movement, utilizing raw, expressive brushwork to challenge conventional academic standards, while further sharpening a precise, graphic sensitivity to human anatomy.
about.section4Text3: The contemporary practice synthesizes these parallel paths into a profound Psychological Realism. The imagery confronts visceral territories across recurring series focused on the grotesque, the anatomy of autopsies, nude portraiture, and modern interpretations of the memento mori. This visual output operates at the definitive intersection of classical reverence and contemporary edge, drawing structural cues from the Old Masters and horror cinema, while being driven by diverse sonic arrangements spanning classical compositions to underground electronic and heavy music textures.
about.section4Text4: Alongside a prolific studio archive of over one thousand professional works, Medvedev channels this technical and academic heritage into an intensive private educational project, Profineart Studio Basel, providing specialized fine art mentorship across the Basel region.
